title: Polydatin: A Promising Natural Compound for HIV-1 Reverse Transcriptase Inhibition with Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Potential
content: The docking study delves into Polydatin's binding affinity (kcal/mol) using molecular docking, specifically targeting HIV-1 reverse transcriptase. TB9, a crystal ligand within HIV-1 reverse transcriptase, displays a low binding energy of -10.7 kcal/mol, suggesting its potential as a target for non-nucleoside inhibition. Polydatin, with a slightly higher binding energy of -9.7 kcal/mol, exhibits significant interaction. Moreover, exploration of Polydatin with other HIV targets, such as HIV-Proteases using the SWISS DOCK Server, reveals its binding to HIV-2 protease and HIV-1 protease. Polydatin's natural origin and potential for low side effects position it as a promising anti-HIV drug candidate, necessitating further studies on pharmacokinetics and toxicity, beyound in vitro and in vivo experiments.
